name: MAXIFS
description: MAXIFS returns the maximum value in a range that meets one or more criteria across corresponding criteria ranges.
tldr: Finds the largest value where multiple conditions are all true.

parameters.name: max_range
parameters.description: The range of cells from which the maximum is returned.

parameters.name: criteria_range1
parameters.description: The first range tested against criteria1; must be the same size as max_range.

parameters.name: criteria_range2, criteria2, ...
parameters.description: Optional additional range/criteria pairs; all must be met (AND logic).

basicExample.description: Largest sale for a specific product
basicExample.explanation: Among rows where column A is Apple, the largest value in column C (e.g. 950) is returned.

advancedExamples.title: Maximum with two criteria
advancedExamples.scenario: Top sale in a region above a threshold
advancedExamples.description: Both conditions must be satisfied (AND logic).
advancedExamples.explanation: Only rows where region is East AND column B exceeds 1000 are considered; the largest such column C value is 1800.

advancedExamples.title: Criterion built from a cell reference
advancedExamples.description: Concatenate a comparison operator with a cell value.
advancedExamples.explanation: If E1 holds 500, this finds the largest column C for Banana where column B is greater than 500, here 1200.

howItWorks: MAXIFS evaluates each criteria_range against its criteria, keeping only the rows where all conditions are true. It then returns the maximum value from max_range at those rows. All ranges must have the same dimensions. If no row satisfies every criterion, MAXIFS returns 0. Criteria support operators (>, <, >=, <=, <>) and wildcards (*, ?) for text. It is the conditional counterpart of MAX, similar to how SUMIFS extends SUM.

howToSteps.name: Select the result cell
howToSteps.text: Click where you want the maximum.

limitations: All ranges must be the same size; mismatched sizes cause #VALUE!.
Applies AND logic only; OR logic across criteria requires separate formulas combined with MAX.
Returns 0 when no row meets all criteria, which can be confused with a real zero.

commonErrors.cause: The criteria ranges and max_range have different sizes or shapes.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure every range covers the same rows and columns.

commonErrors.cause: Criteria text does not exactly match, including case differences or stray spaces.
commonErrors.fix: Use exact text, trim spaces, or use wildcards for partial matches.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports MAXIFS with the same syntax, criteria rules, and AND logic as Excel 2019+.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Returns the largest Apple value, identical to Excel.

faq.question: Can MAXIFS use OR logic?
faq.answer: No, it only applies AND across criteria pairs. For OR, compute separate MAXIFS and wrap them in MAX, or use MAX with FILTER.

faq.question: Why do I get 0?
faq.answer: No row satisfied all criteria, and MAXIFS returns 0 in that case. Check your criteria and ranges.

faq.question: Which Excel versions have MAXIFS?
faq.answer: MAXIFS was introduced in Excel 2019 and is also available in Microsoft 365; it is absent in Excel 2016 and earlier.
